Hero Public Safety Commission.name: Hero Public Safety Commission
Hero Public Safety Commission.basicInfo: The government body that runs the hero system. It writes the rules for hero work, issues and revokes hero licenses, runs the Provisional Hero License Exam and coordinates heroes with the police. It also manages how the public sees heroes: it releases incident statistics, handles press relations and presents the twice-yearly Hero Billboard Chart JP, which ranks heroes by incidents resolved, public approval and social contribution. Its tower in central Tokyo is quiet, efficient and closed to visitors beyond the licensing counter. Heroes depend on it and rarely love it; to most citizens it is a seal on a license. The visible contradiction: a public-safety agency that worries about approval ratings as much as about safety.
Hero Public Safety Commission.hiddenInfo: Behind the counters, the Commission's first concern is public confidence in heroes, not any single case. Senior officials quietly settle hero property-damage claims, keep embarrassing incident reports out of the news and lean on heroes whose conduct hurts the system's image. Clerks and exam proctors believe in the rules they enforce and see little of this; the President and her senior staff decide what stays buried. Pressure is building: the Hero Killer, Stain, has murdered and crippled pro heroes in several cities, and every new attack dents public trust. The Commission shares its Hero Killer files with the police, and its exam office designs the Provisional Hero License Exam anew every year.
